what: The plan sized the whole port at about 23k lines of production C++ plus 7k of tests and bindings, with the receiver about 60% of the work. Stage 0 as built was far larger than its line estimate, because it carries the generated frozen tables.
evidence: port_plan.md: stage 0 1.3k C++ + 0.9k Python; stage 1 4.0k + 1.5k; stage 2 12.3k (2a 5.9k, 2b 2.9k, 2c 3.5k); stage 3 5.0k + 1.4k; plan also names 4 frozen tables of ~27k doubles. Built: stage 0 commit 3843897, 24 files, +7521 lines.

what: Stage 4 (no Python in the app) was deferred in the draft plan and became required after the owner's ruling.
evidence: Draft: 'deferred (about 1.3k)'; after Jeff's 2026-10-13 05:00Z 'no Python in release builds' it became required (~2k). The app swap to the C++ transmitter landed as 2b6d29b at 06:31Z.

what: The plan named churn in the Python receiver as the main schedule risk.
evidence: port_plan.md: 8 receiver commits on 2026-10-11/10-12 cited as the churn risk.

what: Default 9 (audio file format) changed between the draft and the approved plan.
evidence: Draft: write raw .i16 and read FLAC via dr_flac. Approved plan: its own FLAC encoder.

what: The plan's predicted parity tolerances were far looser than what was achieved.
evidence: Predicted: L clipped audio ~1e-9, CE audio 1e-12. Achieved: L clip/frame_baseband max abs 7.9e-16 to 1.33e-15; CE bit-exact on the reference platform (falls back to 1e-12 elsewhere).

what: The plan flagged pybind11 as missing and the venv's onnxruntime 1.31 as differing from the 1.28 pin. The ORT difference turned out to change only error texts.
evidence: Stage-1 codec_cli: the encoder stayed bit-identical across ORT 1.28 and 1.31; only error texts differed.

what: The plan put shared helpers in util/ and io/, but the waves put them under core/qrss/.
evidence: Plan: util/half, io/npz, util/numpy_sum, dsp/upfirdn. Built: core/qrss half, npz, npsum, filters.

what: The plan's task 15 specified new refusals for invalid combinations. Wave 2 implemented check_pilot through ce::check_carrier.
evidence: Plan task 15: refuse L+OOK, an OOK .bin on L, and check_pilot below 322.07 Hz. Follow-up 0f1f9e3: 'check_pilot uses ce::check_carrier'.

what: Stage 1 took about 9 hours of wall time from stage 0, a container restart included.
A container restart interrupted wave 3. Its two lanes were resumed from WIP commits in a rerun workflow.
evidence: wf_8af3e0e3-a7f journal has only 2 'started' lines and no results; WIP commits 584110a and 60b0c73 at 02:55Z; rerun wf_5c80865c-1d3 at 06:02Z.

evidence: Reported by a wave porter (journal notes).

what: Agents share one scratchpad, and one agent overwrote another's probe script.
evidence: Journal notes from wave agents.

what: A worktree started from the wrong base and had to be reset.
evidence: It started at e303a0e, which does not descend from f95c14f.

what: The pybind pattern of a function-local static py::object, found first in filters, also existed in the frame binding.
evidence: Destroyed after interpreter finalization, with a GIL deadlock risk; frame binding fixed in follow-up 0f1f9e3.

what: Python startup costs about 1 s per CLI run, so the CLI parity tests run on 4 threads.
evidence: codec_cli/integrate notes; cli+codec parity 121-134 s.

what: check_includes caught missing standard headers in the new C++.
evidence: std::abs, std::min and <utility> misses caught.

what: Reviewers mutation-checked their regression tests against the pre-fix code.
evidence: codec_cli review: 12 of 148 checks failed against the old code.

what: The adversarial reviews found nearly all bugs at argument boundaries and in refusal texts, and almost none in arithmetic.
evidence: polar/header review: all six fixed findings were argument handling, no arithmetic bug. Similar across frame (13), infra (13) and filters (8).

what: The shared_changes_needed reported by lanes were applied in follow-up commits after each merge.
evidence: f95c14f: PRECODER_BLOCK, sequences binding accepting numpy ints, parity skip. 0f1f9e3: picture/beaconfile/ce/lwave constants generated, lwave uses ce helpers, check_pilot uses ce::check_carrier, frame binding static fixed. 7268bc6: math.fma fallback in the ce test, picture.py docstring.

what: The pytest substitution header grew steadily as modules were ported.
evidence: From 15 substitutions to 160, plus 46 from-import sites, by the end of stage 1.

what: Hand-written ctest pins were wrong twice, each caught on the first ctest run. Every other pin was generated from Python by script and passed first time, so pins should never be typed.
evidence: np.polyfit([1.0],[1.0],1) assumed [1,1], but numpy's minimum-norm answer is [0.5, 0.5] (test_npstats.cpp 'one point, degree 1'). TINY n_sym assumed 1024, actually 1753 (test_ce_rx.cpp "sym has shape (3,), expected (1753,)"). Generator scripts: scratchpad pins.py, fe/pins.py, pins2.py, from infra_testgen splitmix counters.

what: A missing top-level meta key first surfaced as an IndexError from the C++ JSON accessor, which reads like a bug in the port rather than a malformed file. A dedicated pyjson::KeyError, mapped to Python's KeyError and read in Python's key order, makes the first missing key reported ('header') match Python.
evidence: native/core/qrss/pyjson.hpp KeyError; tests/test_qrss_native_types.py missing-key tests

what: The non-slow tier of the named --native-qrss=rx suites barely exercises the receiver. The per-module parity files and smoke/lunits/multipass carry the coverage, while test_qrss_receiver's real coverage is in a slow tier the agents were not allowed to run.
evidence: test_qrss_track.py 5 passed / 8 deselected; test_qrss_receiver.py 4 passed / 55 deselected (wave 4 skeleton review); 'test_qrss_receiver.py's non-slow tier is only 4 tests, so most of its coverage of this lane under --native-qrss=rx comes from the slow tier, which was not run' (wave 5 A1/A2 review)

what: The required 1/64 Hz noise-mask sweep is too slow for the default tier, so it is marked slow. The default tier sweeps at 1/4 Hz and a ctest pins a digest of the one-hertz masks.
evidence: 17,922 positions, about 60 s per band in Python; run once with 0 mismatches. The ctest digest (cd464fb6...) covers 282 one-hertz masks over both bands (99,138 flat bins). The frontend review did not rerun the slow sweep.

what: The worktree sandbox refused compound shell commands (cd plus a heredoc, $PWD, computed command names). The working pattern was to write scripts to the scratchpad with Write and run python on their absolute path.
evidence: several refusals in the frontend lane session; native/tests/qrss/test_*.cpp header comments carry the generating expressions

what: Several parity tolerances were looser than the plan's bar or than what was measured, and reviewers tightened them. A tolerance helper deserves the same adversarial reading as the code it checks.
evidence: Frontend: _fe_close skipped the '<=1e-5 of samples differ' count and exempted parts below 1e-3 of scale; _ch_close/_chan_same added atol 1e-6*max on top of rtol 1e-6 (tightened in commit 42005fa, all still pass). Wave 5 track timing: _carrier_lines was compared to a tolerance though exact, now bitwise. Wave 5 cwid: window tolerance allowed 0.1% of float32 values 1 ulp off against a measured 0, now 1e-4.

what: Several parity files ran near or over the ~40 s per-file budget, especially with agents sharing 4 CPUs. Timings were noisy for the same reason.
evidence: frontend ~35-40 s of a 46.5 s three-file run; track 31.9 s; track_timing 42.8 s, trimmed by cutting the paths probe from 24 to 16 trials; acquire_a12 34.6 s; cwid ~35 s and acquire_tbd ~36 s under shared load. 'normalise ... swinging with machine load' (wave 4 frontend).

what: Bitwise parity checks over signed zeros and ties, plus return-type checks, caught two bugs that the digests and the --native-qrss suites could not.
evidence: std::nth_element in median_filter's generic path returned -0.0 where scipy's NI_Select returns 0.0 (test_qrss_native_ndfilter.py::test_signed_zeros_and_ties); a1_gamma returned a Python float where acquire returns np.float64 (test_qrss_native_acquire_stats.py::test_scalars)

what: Per-function parity on C-contiguous random inputs missed the preamble_p layout bug. Running acquire's real callers with every row monkeypatched and diffing whole results found it on the first run, and wave 5 made this whole-caller A/B mandatory in every parity file.
evidence: test_acquire_end_to_end_on_the_cpp first failed at acquire[2].cell_lam (337.535874989212 vs 337.5358749892118) while the 35 existing parity tests passed. The wave 5 script COMMON requires 'WHOLE-CALLER A/B (required)' with that test as the pattern.

what: A natural-looking erasure fixture tested nothing: erase_s=((5,15),) on TINY lands entirely in the preamble/CW region, so every output equalled the unerased pass. The fixture moved to (25,35) s, and a test now asserts that each fixture has the property its label names. Guard the guard.
evidence: Erased positions 164-495; data starts at 661. tests/qrss_demod_tracks.py; tests/test_qrss_native_demod.py::test_the_tracks_cover_what_they_claim (>100 erased data symbols, header known/unknown, meas mask present).

what: The demod review found the numeric core bit-identical on every probe, and all eight real bugs were in the bindings: how and when arguments are read, and refusals. Reviews should probe argument forms and refusals, not only values.
evidence: tests/qrss_demod_probes.py and test_probe_* in the five parity files: 151 new tests, all passing only after review commits 7ff77c6 and 8e2c4d1 (266 tests, up from 115)

what: A pybind11 binding built a py::float_ inside a py::gil_scoped_release scope, crashing on one path only. Whole-caller tests missed it because the receiver never calls that path; keep the nogil block to the computation and build Python objects after it.
evidence: segfault only on _kf_forward store=False (native/bindings/module/qrss/track.cpp kf_forward_py), found by test_kalman, fixed in ff2f7ba by the port agent

what: Pinning a synthetic end-to-end track() pass in the ctest was cheap and strong. A CE TINY signal over exact-binary-fraction 'noise' reproduces the capture bit for bit in both languages, so q, meas and the decisions are pinned exactly; it also hosts a two-thread reentrancy check.
evidence: native/tests/qrss/test_track.cpp test_synthetic_pass (capture digest 134cbc75...)

what: For a long iterative routine the strongest check is a swap test: assign the C++ versions of the known non-bitwise leaves over the reference's, run the reference, and require bit-for-bit equality. It proves everything downstream is the reference's arithmetic and names each divergence seed; the same idea checked gate V's decision logic.
evidence: test_track_is_the_reference_up_to_smooth_and_templates. Swapping _smooth alone still left P 2.0e-5 on the lead-in call, which revealed SIMD exp in sf as a second seed. test_gate_v_composition: bitwise equality in all 8 scenarios.

what: Absolute tolerances on an ill-conditioned output are fixture luck. The original u/P bounds passed their two fixtures by a 12x margin and failed on the first drifting lead-in scenario probed; the conditional bit-for-bit check is what carries the claim.
evidence: test_track_on_the_receivers_calls held P at 1e-5; test_track_with_a_lead_in measured 2.0e-5 (bound 1e-4 plus the conditional check)

what: Spying on the reference made its internal intermediates checkable without copying its code into the test. The spy replaces the module's np with a proxy that records np.full's 2-D -inf grids and _segment_timing's calls.
evidence: tests/test_qrss_native_track_timing.py _NpSpy and _ref_fit (FFT grid, x, sig2 and peak inputs compared directly)

what: A whole-caller A/B that only compares results with the reference proves nothing if the rows silently never reach the C++. Each A/B must count calls into every native entry point, assert that each row target is the binding, and check that callers beyond receive_pass are reached; reviewers added this in every wave 5 lane.
evidence: A1/A2: call counters and target-is-binding assertions; preamble_search count >= 20 in the acquire A/B; without them both A/Bs would pass on pure Python. Track timing: receive_pass alone never reached receiver._gate's second verify_track or em.pass_path; the test now asserts verify == 2 + len(gates), verify_track == len(gates) + 2*len(refs), line_path == refine_path == len(refs). A3/cwid: spies prove track_before_detect, _hit_to_detection, frame_map, keying_type, window_soft, window_llr, read and match ran.

what: The brief's cwid A/B, receive_pass on CE TINY, would have been vacuous. TINY frames have no callsign windows, so cwid is never called; the A/B runs on SHORT and L_SHORT instead and is marked slow.
evidence: receiver._cw_result: `if spec.n_win == 0: return None, None`; slow receive_pass A/B ce-short 7.3 s, l-short 6.7 s

what: Claiming bit-exactness on a numpy reduction requires knowing which kernel numpy dispatches to at this version. einsum's optimize path, np.angle and float32 np.log all leave the C library, and two of the three were found only by bit-level probes, not by reading the Python.
evidence: scratchpad einprobe.py; test_numpys_float32_log

what: The receive-pass A/Bs compared Detection.uid exactly, but uid hashes the float32 z, so a 1e-13 Hz detection shift can flip it. The exact uid comparison was dropped, as cpp-port-plan 4.1 requires.
evidence: test_receive_pass_on_the_cpp edit (A1/A2 review); track core: 'A pass_uid's sha8 suffix may differ (it hashes float32 z)'

what: pybind11 without stl.h compiles fine but fails at runtime when a std::vector is passed to py::object.attr(...), such as reshape. Build shapes as py::tuple explicitly.
evidence: first parity run: 'Unable to convert call argument' on reshape; fixed with shape_tuple() in both binding files

what: A synthetic OOK callsign stub must key the carrier in the plain units too, not only in key-down units. Without it read_ml on the OOK stub reads garbage while the FSK test passes, which looks like a port bug.
evidence: Plain units are 0-4 and 184-191. scratchpad dbg_ook.py; the fixed stub reads K1ABC (gen_pins.py line 125).

what: Peak memory of one call inside a long-lived Python process can be measured without tracemalloc's overhead: write '5' to /proc/self/clear_refs to reset VmHWM, then read VmHWM after the call.
evidence: scratchpad time_full.py; used for the +202 MB vs +100 MB track_before_detect figures

what: Building a synthetic FULL capture is the slow part of any FULL-slot test. Cos/sin of exactly reduced turns plus a power-of-two FFT halved it, and the FULL-slot test stays slow-tier with the same sizes kept in the fast tier as matrices.
evidence: np.exp of a 7 M complex array plus an odd-length ifft took 13.6 s, against about 6 s for the reduced-turns version on this VM. Fast-tier test_full_size_pieces ~2 s; slow test_track_before_detect_full_slot 13 s.

what: In a whole-caller A/B, install the spies on the native entry points before rows(q) is built, or rows that bind native functions at build time escape them. Also compute the reference's detections before the rows are applied: Acquisition.detections is replaced at class level, so calling it afterwards silently compares native with native.
evidence: tests/test_qrss_native_acquire.py: test_acquire_whole_caller precomputes 'want' before _every_row

what: The isolated-worktree Bash guard refuses chains such as 'git add && git commit && pytest' and 'mv; pytest; mv; git status'. Run each git command on its own.
evidence: Two refusals in the acquire-arbitration session

what: A counting spy over a class row (_Model) must subclass it. A plain function wrapper breaks isinstance and attribute access, so it would silently test a different object than the receiver uses.
evidence: tests/test_qrss_native_ltrack.py _counted

what: The l-tiny lead-in pass, marked slow, runs in 1.7 s and is the only configuration that reaches _lead_supported_l, so it moved to the fast tier. A slow-only mark would have left that row unexercised in the default run.

what: Probing numpy's edge semantics turned up 0-d results that must be numpy scalars, not 0-d arrays (pilot_filter, _pilot_gain, data_mix at a scalar index), and row refusals with their own messages instead of numpy's. The port agent found and fixed four such row bugs itself (shaped_result helper). Only a test comparing type(), not just dtype and shape, catches the first kind.

what: The receivers' fixtures never blank a symbol (keep's mean is 1.0), so psi never fell below PSI_MIN. The erase branches of _Model.streams and the pilot measurement, and _hold_ends with interior infinite R, were untested until the ltrack review's blanked fading probe.

evidence: The first run of test_probe_track_l_from_threads failed only on z_ref nan != nan

what: Parity tests skip under --native-qrss=rx, because they need the reference unsubstituted. With the flag, '-k probe' reports '8 skipped', which reads like success at a glance. Run them without the flag.
evidence: pytest --native-qrss=rx tests/test_qrss_native_ltrack.py -k probe: 8 skipped; acquire parity file 15 skipped

what: A whole-caller A/B can only show that a row is reached and correct when that row's caller stays Python. With every row installed, the C++ verify_l never calls the Python-visible fit_timing_l or resid_ratio. CONFIGS that keep verify_l, then verify_track_l, then fit_timing_l in Python each caught a mutated row.
evidence: Pytest-plugin mutation check: 4 mutants (fit_timing_l, _segment_timing_l, _lag_phase shifted, resid_ratio scaled), each caught in exactly the config that keeps its caller

what: Building the from-import site list from sys.modules by object identity found cwid.rx_index and ltrack's PathFn and freq_path_spline. The hand-written list in the track_timing test had missed them.
evidence: Sites dump: ltrack 38 names including PathFn and freq_path_spline; cwid rx_index

what: Exact orchestration parity is cheap with deterministic stubs. When every stage is a stub whose answer depends only on its question, the C++ reaches them as seams, and call logs (with argument types) and results compare exactly. That gives fast-tier coverage of branches that real captures reach only in slow runs.
evidence: test_acquire_orchestration_stubbed: 240 seeds in about 2.3 s, against about 1-5 s per real acquisition; at least 10 offset triples, 300+ preamble hits and 100+ hinted lines

what: The first wave 6b run was stopped by accident mid-tests. Its WIP commits survived in the worktree, and a resumed agent got a RESUME prompt naming them, read the WIP diff and finished the work. The notes count this as the third time 'commit early' paid off. Wave 6b then merged with no conflicts.
evidence: wf_6a5030c8-827 agent ends '[Request interrupted by user]'; qrss-cpp-wave6b.js RESUME1 (worktree-wf_6a5030c8-827-1, HEAD cb7a31d, two WIP commits 345e006 and cb7a31d on 40c3910); w6b_insights_entries.py section 5

what: The strong swap test runs every receiver function as the reference's, glue included, over the native primitives, and is bit-exact. That pins every remaining difference to a primitive measured in its own parity file. The weak form (only receive_pass as the reference) also passes bit for bit.
evidence: tests/test_qrss_native_receiver.py test_receive_pass_composition 'all/prep' variants, on tiny-6, drift, short-6, l-tiny-6, l-ppm+100 and l-short-6 (the review added v1 SHORT and heavy erase)

what: The receiver parity file's fast tier first ran 93-107 s, because each SHORT reference receive_pass is 4 s of Python. Moving the pure-reference SHORT passes to slow, caching captures and native passes separately, and shrinking the options matrix brought it to about 43 s. SHORT bit-exactness stays in the fast tier through the cheaper composition test.
evidence: 51 passed in 107 s, then 42 passed in 43 s

what: A whole-caller test's scenario assumption was wrong, not the port: a CE Neighbour's header is drawn at random and never decodes, even at 0 dB, though its callsign reads. The joint SHORT test now asserts the L header and the neighbour's callsign.

what: Running a scratch script with 'uv run python' in a worktree that has no .venv silently creates a new 4-package .venv there (no pytest), which then fails on import. Use the main checkout's .venv/bin/python with SSTVAE_NATIVE_MODULE_DIR pointing at the worktree's build.
evidence: First L timing run: ModuleNotFoundError: pytest after 'Creating virtual environment at: .venv'

what: test_qrss_receiver.py has only 4 non-slow tests (55 slow), and the QRSS acceptance file had all 18 tests slow, so '--native-qrss=rx -m not slow' barely reaches the native receiver end to end. The parity files' fast tiers and chosen slow node ids are what actually cover it.

what: The typed/Python-mode switch must identify rows by where they are defined (module plus rows.<locals>.name), never by the __qrss_native__ mark. Spies copy that mark, so trusting it would skip the spy and break the whole-caller reach assertions.
evidence: tests/qrss_native/receiver_slot.py _defined_in/_typed

evidence: 2671a6b: tests/test_qrss_native_receiver.py _counted 'if key[0] != RECEIVER or not callable(fn)'

what: CLAUDE.md said a SHORT pass is 10-15 s, which was stale at wave 6b: Python receive_slot on SHORT CE took 4.0 s, joint 7.3 s, and 1.6 s in C++.
evidence: Measured 4.04 s / 7.29 s (receiver-slot port). CLAUDE.md now reads '10-15 s each at the time'.

Wave 7 brought it to 33 s by keeping one typed CE, L and joint scenario, a Python-mode run with spies, the typed-stays-typed assertions and the whole-caller test with every _SLOT_ROWS reached (10.6 s), and moving the 9 other scenarios, dets_given, ce_resid_ratio, finish_receive (12 s), scenarios_reach_the_rules and threads to slow.

A grammar fuzz of chunk orders, lying sizes and truncations, plus a direct _read_wav window compared bitwise with warnings, is what reached them. what: The CLI's codec-only sources need a CMake decision: the glob covers apps/sstvae_qrss/*.cpp and filters only encode.cpp. --image was verified with a temporary, reverted CMake hook and wired in at the merge. A wave that adds codec-dependent CLI code should name CMakeLists.txt as editable.

what: Running the side-by-side CLI cases in a 4-way thread pool keeps the fast tier at 32-39 s while still running 2 Python SHORT receives and 24 Python refusal runs. The L, noise and old-rules cases went to a 28 s slow test, and FULL --image is two slow tests (44-48 s each).
evidence: pytest --durations on tests/test_qrss_native_cli_receive.py

what: zipfile.ZipFile.writestr stamps the current local time, whereas ZipFile.open(name, 'w') (what np.savez uses) stamps 1980-01-01. A hand-built archive in a pin generator therefore made the committed pins nondeterministic until switched.
evidence: Two runs of gen_simfile_pins.py differed at simfile_pins.hpp:1325 (efbc4d5d vs b8bb4d5d); fixed by z.open(k, 'w', force_zip64=True)

what: The decimal-comma locale test is layered redundantly and cannot detect a single regression: main.cpp resets LC_NUMERIC after QCoreApplication adopts the environment, and frame::py_format independently maps any locale decimal point to '.'. In a build without the fetcher it holds by construction. A py_format locale ctest was suggested.
evidence: A mutant main.cpp without the reset passed pytest -k locale; a Qt 6.4.2 probe printed 'after LC_NUMERIC: de_DE.UTF-8 ... 1,50'

what: Wave 7 merged with no conflicts, and stage 2 is done. --native-qrss=rx fast tier green on every QRSS suite, the reverse chain (Python transmits, C++ receives) tested, A-7 rechecked with no constant moving, and statistical acceptance against 13 committed references with hash pins on 30+ sources.
evidence: w7_insights_entries.py section 5; pushed c0c830f

what: Reviews kept finding tests that could not fail: the cw.agrees JSON test, a runners-up test that counted candidates but not which timings were tracked, and a CRLF test that re-implemented the normalisation it claimed to cover. Mutation-checking each new test is the habit that caught all three.
evidence: review:reference-fixes findings 0-1; review:acceptance finding 1

what: A slow test run by node id without -m slow is silently deselected ('1 deselected', exit 0 through a pipe), because pyproject's addopts deselects slow. Always pass -m slow with the node id.
evidence: First run of test_noise_slots_on_the_cpp[tiny] printed only '1 deselected in 0.09s'

what: Two hazards in background work. A waiter 'until ! pgrep -f "ninja -C ... sstvae_native"' never exits, because pgrep -f matches the waiter's own command line; wait on a pid or a marker file. And the scratchpad is shared between concurrent agents: another agent's build log overwrote this one, so keep a per-task subdirectory.
evidence: Task b6g7nop2y still running long after ninja finished; build1.log overwritten

what: The 60 SHORT noise slots did not fit one 3-minute node id and were split into short-1 and short-2. Half of each slot's cost is _listen re-running acquisition in Python to count A2/A3 hits, since the typed C++ receive_slot does not expose its Acquisition. A binding that returned it would halve the cost; not done.
evidence: First [short] run timed out at 200 s; halves 110-133 s; each slot about 2.8 s C++ plus 5-9 s on the reference

what: Moving a refusal earlier in a script breaks every parity test that reached a later refusal through that script. Grep for every test reaching the old refusal before calling the change done.
evidence: tests/test_qrss_native_api.py, not on the task's list, failed 4 cases (q=-1) after parse_slot started refusing pre-1970; fixed in 4277897

what: Timings taken while other agents share the 4 CPUs were off by up to 4x. Only pinned, repeated runs (OMP/BLAS threads 1, first run discarded) gave usable before/after numbers.
evidence: ab_before.log 3.15 s vs bench_acq.py 0.838-1.01 s for the same CE SHORT acquire

what: The codec tree's first build (160 steps, -j2) took 9.5 min, just under the 600 s cap. A later lane touching core headers is safer reusing it incrementally than reconfiguring.
